baseline.procedure: Open the page fresh (new browser context, empty localStorage), click #resetBtn, then set every control listed below even if it already shows the value. Money inputs (.money-input, e.g. #propertyPrice) accept digits; type the value and blur so a change event fires. Sliders (input[type=range]) must be set to the exact value and dispatch an input event; confirm via the neighbouring .slider-value span. Segmented controls (.seg-group) are set by clicking the .seg-btn whose data-val is given. Do NOT press any Quick Start city button.

tab_general.#initialCash: (leave blank: the page's own sub-label says it defaults to down payment + setup cost)

read_rules.series: Yearly series come from the detail tables (#detailTableWrap; tabs .tab-btn[data-table=own], [data-table=rent], [data-table=rtb]) or, equivalently, from the CSV export (#downloadBtn) - the two must agree. 'Year N' is the row labelled year N, i.e. the state at the END of year N. If a year-0 row exists use it for year-0 quantities; otherwise year-0 cash is: Own = initial cash - down payment - setup cost, Rent (and RTB before purchase) = initial cash, and the year-0 loan balance is the loan taken (property price - down payment).
read_rules.outflow: 'outflow' of a path in a year = every amount the path pays out in that year: for Own/RTB-after-purchase the FULL mortgage repayments (interest and principal) plus all ongoing costs (plus a principal/balloon repayment only where an observable says to include it); for Rent, rent plus rent ongoing costs. It is NOT the 'Accum. Cost' figure, which may leave out principal.
read_rules.budget: 'budget' of a path in a year = the yearly housing budget the table shows as credited to that path for that year (what the path receives before paying its outflow). If the table has no budget column use the CSV's; if neither exists report null and say so in notes.
read_rules.cash: 'cash' = the liquid cash / investment balance of the path at the end of the year (the Liquid Cash series).
read_rules.netEquity: 'net equity' of a path at year N = the value the Net Equity series/table shows for that path at year N.
read_rules.loanBalance: 'loan balance' at the end of year N = the outstanding mortgage principal shown for that year; if the table shows property value and property equity instead, balance = property value - property equity.
read_rules.kpis: KPI values are parsed from #kpiInitialCash, #kpiBudgetRange (two figures: min and max), #kpiBreakeven and #kpiDiff. Report every currency amount as a plain number (no symbol, no thousands separators, '-' for negatives). For #kpiBreakeven report the integer year; if the KPI says owning never overtakes renting within the horizon (any wording such as a dash, 'Never', 'N/A', 'beyond horizon') report null; if it says owning is ahead from the start report 1.
read_rules.residuals: Observables named '...Residual...' or '...MaxAbs' are computed by the runner from the named page quantities exactly as written, using the risk-free rate entered as rf (e.g. 4.5% -> 0.045).
read_rules.nan: 'nanCount' = number of visible KPI values, snapshot tiles, legend/hover entries and table cells whose text contains NaN, Infinity, undefined or null.

setup.note: Detailed mortgage mode (#mortgageModeGroup data-val=detailed) reveals #mortgageTypeRow (radios name=mortgageType value pi|io, checkbox #costInterestOnly) and #rateScheduleRow. observe.what: Base schedule (one fixed period years 1-30 at 6.0%): number in #kpiDiff.
Edit 1: add a second fixed period years 31-35 at 9.0% (term stays 30). #kpiDiff after the edit minus kpiDiffBase.

Edit 2 (fresh base, then): periods [1-10 @ 6.0], [5-15 @ 8.0], [16-30 @ 6.0], all fixed. Classify the resulting #kpiDiff: 'later-wins' if it equals (within 1) the #kpiDiff of the non-overlapping schedule [1-4 @ 6.0],[5-15 @ 8.0],[16-30 @ 6.0]; 'first-wins' if it equals that of [1-10 @ 6.0],[11-15 @ 8.0],[16-30 @ 6.0]; 'rejected' if the page refused the overlapping entry (validation message, bounds auto-corrected, or the row reverted) and the value equals kpiDiffBase; otherwise 'other'. Record the three values and any message in notes.

Edit 3 (fresh base, then): periods [1-4 @ 6.0], one entered with from-year 10 and to-year 5 at 8.0, [11-30 @ 6.0]. Classify #kpiDiff: 'normalised' if it equals (within 1) the #kpiDiff of [1-4 @ 6.0],[5-10 @ 8.0],[11-30 @ 6.0]; 'rejected' if the page refused or ignored the reversed period and the value equals kpiDiffBase; otherwise 'other'.

Edit 4 (fresh base, then): periods [1-15 @ 6.0], [16-30 @ 8.0]; THEN set #mortgageTerm to 15. #kpiDiff after that, minus the #kpiDiff of a fresh setup with #mortgageTerm 15 and a single period [1-15 @ 6.0].

Edit 5 (fresh base, then): one floating period 1-30 entered with low 7.0 / mid 6.0 / high 5.0 (backwards). Take the three band verdicts (as in R5.verdictBandLowMidHigh), sort them ascending; do the same for the band entered as low 5.0 / mid 6.0 / high 7.0; report the largest absolute element-wise difference.
